Detailed appeals were lodged; appeal hearings took place 12–15 June 2023 (panel including Mr Whitehead) and outcomes were communicated by letters dated 15–16 June 2023. The claimants lodged unfair dismissal claims in June 2023 and a final ET hearing was listed in Edinburgh on 18–22 August and 6–7 November 2025; the respondent was represented by Ms E Campbell and the claimants took the lead in proceedings themselves.

facts: The respondent is a plastic recycling business employing around 40 people. The claimant was employed as a process operator from 8 August 2022 until dismissal for gross misconduct on 30 January 2025. After a non-workplace assault on 24 November 2024, the claimant sustained a finger injury and submitted a series of fit notes. On 10 January 2025, one fit note said he may be fit for work with workplace adaptations, but a later fit note stated he was not fit for work for six weeks. The respondent arranged meetings and an occupational health assessment; the claimant did not attend a meeting on 16 January 2025 or the disciplinary hearing on 30 January 2025. The respondent treated the matter as concerning absence from work and dishonesty in receiving sick notes, and dismissed him for gross misconduct.

facts: Mr Snaith had been employed by Aurorium UK Limited since June 2008 and became Europe Finance Director in January 2022, with financial oversight of the United Kingdom, Belgium, Austria and the Netherlands. Aurorium Netherlands had a Rabobank loan agreement containing a covenant restricting loans to group companies, and the claimant received a copy of that agreement in February 2022 but did not read it or seek advice on it. Between October 2023 and January 2024, Aurorium Netherlands made €7.8m of inter-company loans to Aurorium Austria, which breached the covenant. Rabobank later declined to renew the financing, creating a shortfall of approximately $12m and prompting an internal investigation.

facts: Ms Dawn Piper worked for the Respondent from 1993 until her resignation on 27 September 2024 and held the position of Senior Sales Manager from 2009. From October 2022 her line manager was Mr Andrew McLuckie, and she managed a small team while also carrying a substantial personal sales portfolio. On 1 August 2024 the Respondent introduced the H2 REM commission scheme, under which Sales Managers' own-sales commission depended on passing four Sales Leadership Compliance Gateways. The Claimant learned of the scheme on 12 August 2024, raised concerns about its financial impact, and estimated that the changes could reduce her earnings by about 70-75%. On 11 September 2024 she was told she had failed Gateways 1 and 2 and would not receive August commission, but following a challenge her August commission was paid in the September payroll. On 23 August 2024 she discovered that £449.22 had been deducted from her July commission because of an incorrect customer email address.

ground_truth_outcome.unapportioned_reason: Liability-only judgment; remedy deferred to a separate hearing.
